datasets.name: KDDCup-99 Intrusion

win_claim.quote: SMOTEBoost applied to several highly and moderately imbalanced data sets shows improvement in prediction performance on the minority class and overall improved F-values.

uncertain: Condition choice: SMOTE and SMOTEBoost are each reported at N = 100/200/300/500 (KDD: Nu2r = 100/300/500); no single N designated main. Chose N = 100 for both (first reported). Pp.7-8.
best_other_value taken as max printed F-value over Standard RIPPER, Standard Boosting, First SMOTE then Boost (all N) and AdaCost (all c), not restricted to N = 100. Pp.7-8.
KDDCup-99: Table 2 counts are the new test set distribution (p.6); n_instances left null (69,980 is the sampled total before splitting, not printed in Table 2).
KDDCup-99 has two minority classes (U2R, R2L); n_minority/n_majority left null; only U2R results reported (R2L omitted 'due to space limitations', p.7).
Mammography and Phoneme source_repo/how_obtained: paper only cites [1] and [23]; no repository or class construction stated (p.6).
Tables 3-6 were interleaved in text extraction; values read from rendered pages 7-8 (is_image set true for that reason, though PDF has a text layer).
Task labelled 'both' because KDDCup-99 is 5-class while others are 2-class; results reported per minority class only (p.6-7).
notes: Proposed method SMOTEBoost (variant of AdaBoost.M2 with SMOTE in each round), base learner RIPPER. Evaluation: 10-fold CV for mammography, satimage, phoneme; separate test set for KDDCup-99 (p.6). Only recall, precision, F-value for minority class are reported; no G-mean or AUC. Precision and recall also reported per setting in Tables 3-6. SMOTE parameter N ranged 100-500. Text p.10 gives relative F-value improvements of SMOTEBoost over AdaBoost.M1: U2R ~4%, R2L 0.61%, mammography 2.2%, satimage 3.4%, phoneme 1.4% (vs boosting, not SMOTE). Figs 2-4 plot precision/recall/F-value over boosting rounds (incl. 'SMOTE applied on RIPPER' line). n_features not printed for any dataset.
